result:
I found 9 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't follow their docstrings, and fixed all of them. To confirm, I parsed every docstring for all 150 rules (type, percentage, threshold and cap) and computed the expected price from those values. I then compared each function against that across quantities 0–259 plus some large values, unit prices from 0 to about 1,000,003, and negative inputs. Before the fix 9 rules failed; after it, none do.

| Rule | Docstring | What it actually did | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02 | 3% | 4% discount | `base * 3 // 100` |
| 27 | 7%, discount capped at 100,000 won | Capped the price at 100,000 before taking 7% | Compute the 7% discount first, then cap it |
| 54 | 7% | 8% discount | `base * 7 // 100` |
| 67 | Discount rounded down to the won | Used `round()`, which rounds to nearest and goes through decimals | `base * 12 // 100` |
| 72 | 5% | 6% discount | `base * 5 // 100` |
| 128 | Discount capped at 50,000 won | Cap only applied when the discount was over 100,000, so discounts between 50,000 and 100,000 went through uncapped | Always `min(disc, 50000)` |
| 142 | Same as 128 | Same as 128 | Same as 128 |
| 145 | 3%, discount capped at 10,000 won | Capped the price at 10,000 before taking 3% | Compute the 3% discount first, then cap it |
| 146 | Discount from 12 units up | Discount started at 13 units (`qty > 12`) | `qty >= 12` |

Rules 105 and 106 also use `qty > threshold`, but I left them alone. They are "marginal" rules (the discount applies only to units above the threshold), so at exactly the threshold the discount is 0 either way. Their results already match the docstrings.

The original file is backed up at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py` and the check script is at `/tmp/chk/check.py`.

STATUS: DONE
